label: The Martyrdom of Polycarp is addressed to the church sojourning at Philomelium

date.note: The Letter of the Smyrnaeans (Martyrdom of Polycarp) was written soon after Polycarp's death. The majority dating, fixed by the proconsulship of Statius Quadratus, is c. 155-156; the Eusebian chronicle places the martyrdom under Marcus Aurelius, c. 166-167. The range brackets both.

primary.cite: Martyrdom of Polycarp, salutation: 'The Church of God which sojourns at Smyrna, to the Church of God sojourning at Philomelium'

secondary.cite: Harnack, Mission and Expansion, vol. 2, p. 188; synopsis at p. 95

notes: The letter is sent from the church at Smyrna to the church at Philomelium (Phrygia Paroreios, mod. Aksehir), a contemporary attestation of a congregation there c. 155-167. Harnack (p. 188) cites 'the epistle of the Smyrniote church upon Polycarp's death.' The Greek names the recipient as the church paroikouse Philomelion, sojourning at Philomelium.
